findings.claim: The new binding-unverified control changes two variables at once, so a refusal it ever produces would not be attributable to the missing execution evidence. plant_unverified_boot_entry writes the entry to <tmp>/unverified-entry.py and only reads bytes out of ROOT; it never places the artifact's ops/conductor/tools directory on sys.path. Every other boot invocation in the suite runs entry = <artifact>/ops/conductor/tools/lane_mcp.py (support:1240-1241, argv built at 1247), which puts that tools directory on sys.path[0]. Modules in that artifact directory are imported flat between siblings -- the D-A31 receipt shows exactly that failure mode when the artifact root rather than the tools directory is on the path: `lane_refs.py line 25, from lane_read import ...` -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'lane_read'. So this control differs from the binding-mismatch control at snapshots:458-471 in both the load evidence and the import environment. If the flat import fails first, the case never reaches the binding gate and the assertEqual at snapshots:490-495 fails on the wrong cause; if it does refuse, the missing evidence is not the isolated variable. The exact-refusal assertion the ruling demanded is present and correct -- this is about the scenario feeding it. I did not open lane_mcp.py (declared limit), so I state the sys.path asymmetry, which is provable from test bytes, not a claim about that module's imports.

findings.claim: The F5 correction removes four vacuous assertions elsewhere and adds three here. measure_eight_card_headroom (discovery_v3_support.py:1751-1816) already asserts eight <= START_CAP at 1802-1807 and headroom >= 0 at 1811, and builds its return dict with the literal "cap": START_CAP at 1814. startup:289 re-asserts the first, startup:291 re-asserts the second (and it is implied by the first), and startup:290 assertEqual(measured["cap"], START_CAP) compares a constant against the same constant the helper just wrote one line earlier -- it cannot fail for any subject, any fixture, or any implementation. Separately, `nine` is computed at support:1798-1800 and no assertion in either file consumes it. The measurement itself is sound and is the one corrected predicate that actually executes: D-A38b fails at startup.py:294 (self.start()), after the headroom measurement at 288 has run and passed, so the eight-cards-fit premise is now measured rather than asserted, exactly as F5 required. The finding is the three added lines, not the measurement.

findings.claim: The failed-before-phase control closes the multiset but not the clause that governs it. discovery-lever.md:334-336 requires "Failed-before-phase and early-stop fixtures must account for each omitted event by its observed failure, not silently accept a missing callback." The control plants the failure (destroy_head_object at adapter:326) and then asserts only the empty eligible multiset via assert_checkpoint_closure (334-339) plus assertIsNotNone(failed) (340). Nothing inspects `failed` for the repo source's state or reason, so an implementation that emitted no repo checkpoint because it silently skipped the source -- rather than because it failed before the phase -- satisfies the whole control; assertIsNotNone accepts any object. The sibling disabled control at 306-321 has the same shape but its omission is accounted for by the planted config, which is a declared cause. F1's named remedies (exact eligible multiset, per-source traces, missing and extra controls, the declared partial order with no cross-source total order) are all discharged; this is the adjacent contract sentence left open.

envelope.note:
Reviewer: Claude Opus 5, Claude Code harness, read profile with Python execution. Scope: the seven discovery_v3 files at 2e93ae6 against 710dbac, rechecked after the F1-F6 ruling.

Verdict: changes, on one blocker that is not about the ruling at all.

The ruling is discharged. All six corrections do what F1-F6 asked, and I verified each against the contract bytes rather than against the producer's word. F1: the eligible multiset model matches discovery-lever.md:315-322 term for term, Counter equality rejects both missing and extra pairs, and it is applied to all four cases including an empty-Counter failed-before-phase control; the partial order is asserted per source and never across sources. F2: the stationary neighbour now runs the identical nested walk, negated. F3: the exact binding-unverified line is pinned with assertEqual beside the mismatch and clean controls, and the token is asserted rather than merely declared. F4: D-A42 captures owned_surface ahead of the refusal, the two handoffs self-checks are gone without losing the occurrences coverage beside them, and the closed-enum ownership check is kept as the ruling directed. F5: the eight-card premise is measured through the independent envelope model, and it is the one corrected predicate that actually executes - D-A38b fails at startup.py:294, after the measurement passed. F6: both faulty controls now consume fixture evidence and carry contrasting failures, while still accepting the planted fault, which was their point.

Everything the brief asked me to preserve is preserved, measured not assumed. All seven final sha256s equal the producer's declared block; all five original sha256s at 6bd91ba equal the values the original report cited, so the corrections were built on the bytes the ruling names. The diff is byte-identical to a regenerated one. 53 row IDs across 56 methods, none lost or invented. The thirteen prior fixes are untouched. No skips, sleeps or randomness. The combined red reproduces exactly - Ran 56, failures=62, zero ERROR lines - and so do all six focused per-file receipts, independently run.

The blocker is lint. ops/devlane/workflow/checks/lint.py is a registered CI gate (gate-kinds/tdd.json:57-58, ci: true) and it is red here: two ruff findings, B023 in support and S103 in adapter. Neither code appears in ruff.toml's per-file-ignores for ops/conductor/tests/*.py, neither line carries a noqa, and ruff 0.16.5 is inside the pinned range, so this is a real verdict. The producer's description is true in its own frame - both were present at 6bd91ba, and startup, handoffs and snapshots are individually clean - but against 710dbac all seven files are new, whole-tree ruff finds exactly these two and nothing else, and the gate returns 1. Assertion-red on the tests is the intended state; a red lint gate is not, and is cheap to clear either with a noqa carrying its reason or a ruff.toml row.

Three p3s follow, none of which would reject a conforming implementation. The binding-unverified scenario changes the import environment as well as the load evidence, so a refusal it produces would not be attributable to the missing evidence alone. D-A38b adds three assertions that cannot fail, one of them comparing a constant to the same constant the helper just wrote - the class F4 asked to remove. And the failed-before-phase control asserts the empty multiset but never inspects the result for the failure that is supposed to explain it, which discovery-lever.md:334-336 requires by name.

Limits, declared. 58 of the 62 failures are the runtime rejecting --discovery-boot-fd as an unknown verb, inside load_envelope, before any row's own predicates. Only F5 is reached at runtime; D-A31 dies at adapter.py:251, D-A47 at snapshots.py:296, D-A42 at adapter.py:439, so every judgement on F1, F2, F3, F4 and F6 is a static read of the fixtures, not an observed discrimination. The four non-boot failures are unchanged from the prior round and I report them as read without claiming which are runtime and which are fixture. I did not open any implementation source or the GPT-6 candidate, did not run ops/bin/suites.sh, launched no vendor, touched no state or admission, and edited nothing; git status --porcelain is empty at the snapshot root after every run.
